justify_why_gaps_are_missing.justification: X-axis shows Lag (hours) with regularly spaced tick labels (approx. 24–48 h); no sudden numeric jumps or compressed regions indicating an omitted range.
Y-axis (Rhythmicity index) tick spacing and numeric sequence are continuous and regular across the plotted range; no evidence of an unlabeled break.
X-axis (Circadian component, 0–1) has evenly spaced ticks and continuous numeric progression; no omitted segment.
Y-axis is on a log scale (Log10 noise) but shows continuous tick progression appropriate for log scaling; there is no abrupt jump or visual axis break that would require an explicit break marker.

Top density plot x-axis (Period, ~21–33 h) and bottom density x-axis (log(amplitude)) use continuous scales appropriate to the data; ticks progress continuously (bottom panel uses a logarithmic axis) with no omitted ranges.
Density axes show continuous density values with no discontinuities or jumps that would indicate an omitted section.
X-axis lists categorical cell lines; categorical axes do not require axis-break markers and show no omitted categories.
Y-axis (ridge length in hours) shows a continuous numeric scale from high to low with regular tick spacing; no abrupt numeric jump or visual break.
Polar histograms are circular (angle = phase) and naturally wrap from 2π to 0; this circular continuity does not require an axis break marker.
Radial (probability) axis is continuous and does not show omitted ranges or jumps that would need a break indicator.
Overall polar histogram uses continuous angular scaling (phase) with natural wrap; no axis-break marking is required.
Radial/probability axis is continuous without omitted segments or discontinuities.
Time axis (hours) is continuous from ~0 to >100 with regular tick spacing; no omitted time intervals or sudden jump requiring a break marker.
Signal axis shows continuous amplitude values without abrupt numeric jumps or compressed zones that would indicate a hidden axis segment.
X-axis (amplitude exponential decay rate, γ) shows a continuous numeric progression (likely linear or log-scaled depending on ticks) without abrupt numeric gaps that would require a break.

Y-axis (Amplitude A0) displays a continuous range of values (including a high-value region) but uses standard tick labeling; there is no visual zigzag or other marker indicating an axis break, nor is there an abrupt unsupported numeric jump that would justify an omitted-range marker.
